jobs.description:
Director of Development

Status:
Exempt, Full-Time (40 hours/week)
Salary:
$62,000–$75,000 annually, dependent upon qualifications and experience
Reports To:
Executive Director

About Red Wing Arts

Since 1952, Red Wing Arts has connected people through creativity by providing exhibitions, education, festivals, concerts, public art, and arts experiences that strengthen our community.
Mission:
To build a vibrant community fueled by the arts by connecting, celebrating, inspiring, and leading through shared art experiences.
As Red Wing Arts continues to grow, we are investing in philanthropy as a strategic priority to ensure our long-term sustainability and expand our impact throughout the region.

Position Summary

The Director of Development leads Red Wing Arts' comprehensive development program in partnership with the Executive Director and Board of Directors.
This position is responsible for growing philanthropic support, strengthening relationships with donors and community partners, and building the systems and strategies that support the organization's long-term financial sustainability.
Success in this role is measured by stronger donor relationships, increased philanthropic investment, diversified revenue, effective fundraising systems, and the continued growth of Red Wing Arts' development program.

Areas of Responsibility

1. Build Relationships

Lead the organization's efforts to cultivate, solicit, and steward meaningful relationships with individuals, businesses, foundations, and community partners.
Success in this area includes:

Building and managing an active portfolio of donor and funding relationships.
Increasing donor engagement and long-term stewardship.
Expanding relationships with corporations, foundations, and community partners.
Partnering with the Executive Director and Board to strengthen major gift cultivation and donor engagement.

2. Build the Development Program

Develop, implement, and evaluate a comprehensive development strategy that supports the organization's mission and strategic goals.
Success in this area includes:

Developing and implementing an annual Development Plan.
Establishing fundraising priorities and measurable annual goals.
Growing annual giving, membership, corporate support, foundation funding, and major gifts.
Strengthening donor management systems and stewardship practices.
Building the organizational capacity needed for future comprehensive fundraising initiatives.

3. Strengthen Organizational Capacity

Provide leadership for the systems, communication, and collaboration that support successful fundraising across the organization.
Success in this area includes:

Coordinating grant proposals and reporting in collaboration with staff.
Maintaining accurate donor records and development reporting.
Supporting the Board Development Committee and fundraising efforts of Board members.
Collaborating with staff to communicate the impact of Red Wing Arts and inspire philanthropic investment.

Qualifications

The ideal candidate will bring many of the following qualifications:
Experience leading fundraising, philanthropy, nonprofit development, business development, or relationship management.
Demonstrated success building relationships and securing philanthropic support.
Experience developing and implementing fundraising strategies.
Experience with capital campaigns, including campaign planning, major gift cultivation, matching or challenge gifts, and campaign readiness.
Strong written, verbal, organizational, and interpersonal communication skills.
Experience working collaboratively with boards, volunteers, and community partners.
Knowledge of annual giving, major gifts, grants, corporate partnerships, donor stewardship, and fundraising best practices.

CFRE certification or comparable professional fundraising credentials are welcomed but not required.
We recognize that exceptional candidates bring a variety of professional experiences. If your background does not align perfectly with every qualification listed, but you believe you would thrive in this role and advance the mission of Red Wing Arts, we encourage you to apply.

What Success Looks Like

Within the first two years, the Director of Development will:
Implement a comprehensive Development Plan aligned with the organization's strategic priorities.
Strengthen donor engagement and stewardship practices.
Increase philanthropic support while diversifying contributed revenue.
Build systems that improve fundraising effectiveness and accountability.
Expand Red Wing Arts' long-term fundraising capacity through stronger relationships, sustainable practices, and strategic planning.

Commitment to Inclusion

Red Wing Arts is dedicated to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace. We welcome applications from candidates of all backgrounds and experiences who share our passion for the arts and community building.

How to Apply

Please submit a cover letter and resume to emily@redwingarts.org
.
Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis and the position will remain open until the right candidate is identified.

jobs.description:
Job Description

USF Advancement connects the university with donors who want to make a difference by providing philanthropic support to promote student success, research, academic excellence and other strategic priorities. With an endowment that now exceeds $700 million in value, our dedicated team of approximately 200 professionals, including 60 fundraisers, encompasses alumni, development and foundation operations. The team is responsible for raising more than $150 million annually and has broken records year after year with more than $184 million raised in fiscal year 2025.

The Director of Development is a fundraising professional responsible for securing philanthropic support for Women in Leadership & Philanthropy (WLP) and strategic priorities across the University of South Florida.

Reporting directly to the Assistant Vice President for Affinity Programs and Executive Director of Women in Leadership & Philanthropy, this position is dedicated exclusively to development activities and serves as a key member of the USF Advancement team.

The Director of Development identifies, qualifies, cultivates, solicits, and closes major gifts from individuals, corporations, and foundations. The successful candidate will manage a portfolio of prospects and donors, develop meaningful relationships that advance donor engagement, and partner with university leadership to align philanthropic investments with institutional priorities.

Employees of USF Advancement live out the values of responsibility, innovation, service, and excellence in each of its highly collaborative departments. We use trusted data and ethical AI to enhance decision-making, strengthen engagement, and enable our teams to focus on what matters most: relationships and impact.

This position is primarily onsite and requires flexibility to meet with donors and prospects throughout the Tampa Bay region and beyond.

Responsibilities

Identify, cultivate, solicit and manage a portfolio of major gift prospects and donors ($50,000+) with a focus on securing significant philanthropic support for Women in Leadership & Philanthropy and the University of South Florida.
Identify and qualify new prospects through research, referrals, volunteer engagement, and personal outreach.
Conduct discovery, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship meetings with prospects and donors.
Develop and implement individualized strategies to move prospects through the donor pipeline from identification to gift commitment.
Collaborate with advancement colleagues and university stakeholders to identify philanthropic opportunities and align donor interests with institutional needs.
Prepare proposals, gift agreements and other donor communications that support fundraising objectives.
Maintain accurate records of prospect activity, strategy, and outcomes within university systems.
Meet established activity and fundraising goals, including visits, solicitations, proposal submissions, and gift commitments.
Represent the University of South Florida and Women in Leadership & Philanthropy at donor meetings, events, and community engagements as appropriate.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

This position requires Bachelor's degree and 5 years of experience related to development or other appropriate professional experience. Five to seven years demonstrated experience identifying, cultivating, soliciting, and closing major ($50,000+) philanthropic gifts is preferred.

About Us

Working at USF

With approximately 16,000 employees, the University of South Florida is one of the largest employers in the Tampa Bay area. We are dedicated to cultivating a talented, engaged and driven workforce that strives to be bold. Employees excel in USF‘s rich academic environment, which fosters their development and advancement. In 2025, Forbes recognized USF as one of Florida’s best large employers, ranked No. 1 among the state’s 12 public universities. Our first-class benefits package includes medical, dental and life insurance plans, retirement plan options, employee and dependent tuition programs, generous leave, and hundreds of employee perks and discounts.

About USF

The University of South Florida is a top-ranked research university serving approximately 50,000 students from across the globe at campuses in Tampa, St. Petersburg, Sarasota-Manatee and USF Health. USF is recognized by U.S. News & World Report as a top 50 public university and the best value in Florida. U.S. News also ranks the USF Health Morsani College of Medicine as the No. 1 medical school in Florida and in the highest tier nationwide. USF is a member of the Association of American Universities (AAU), a group that includes only the top 3% of universities in the U.S. With an all-time high of $738 million in research funding in 2024 and as a top 20 public university for producing U.S. patents, USF uses innovation to transform lives and shape a better future. The university generates an annual economic impact of more than $6 billion. USF’s Division I athletics teams compete in the American Athletic Conference. Learn more at www.usf.edu .

jobs.description:
Company Description
Medi Globe America (MGA), established in 2005, is a business development and practice management organization based in St. Louis, Missouri, with additional offices in the United Kingdom and India. The company focuses on developing global markets for American healthcare products and services while providing comprehensive practice management solutions to healthcare organizations across the United States. MGA supports a wide range of organizations, including independent and hospital-affiliated physician practices, ambulatory surgery centers, federally qualified health centers, rural health centers, and home health organizations. Through its services, MGA aims to build operationally efficient, financially strong, and patient-centered outpatient organizations. By expanding global revenue opportunities, the company helps strengthen domestic patient care programs, support job creation, and contribute to the nation’s economic growth.
Role Description
The Managing Director is a full-time, on-site leadership role based in Lakeview, OR, responsible for overseeing Medi Globe America’s strategic, operational, and financial performance. This individual will lead business development initiatives for global healthcare markets, guide practice management service delivery, and ensure alignment with organizational goals and client expectations. Day-to-day responsibilities include setting strategic direction, managing key client relationships, coordinating cross-functional teams, and monitoring performance metrics for both global market development and practice management services. The Managing Director will oversee budgets, resource allocation, and process improvements, while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and patient-centered service. This role also involves representing MGA with external partners and stakeholders, identifying new growth opportunities, and ensuring compliance with relevant regulations and organizational policies.
Qualifications

Demonstrated leadership experience in healthcare, business development, or practice management, with a track record of managing teams and complex projects.
Strong strategic planning and decision-making skills, including experience with market expansion, revenue growth initiatives, and operational improvement.
Proficiency in managing client relationships, negotiating partnerships, and communicating effectively with executive stakeholders and clinical leaders.
Solid understanding of healthcare operations, revenue cycle management, and front and back office processes in physician practices or similar organizations.
Excellent analytical, financial management, and budgeting skills, with the ability to interpret data and use insights to drive performance.
Ability to work on-site in Lakeview, OR, collaborate across diverse teams and geographies, and adapt to evolving organizational and market needs.
Bachelor’s degree in business, healthcare administration, or a related field; advanced degree (MBA, MHA) or equivalent experience is preferred.
Experience in international business or global healthcare markets is highly beneficial, along with familiarity with regulatory and compliance requirements.

Draft and oversee various IFA communications channels including newsletters, websites, columns, and social media in conjunction with IFA’s marketing team
Lead on executive communications and positioning for IFA President and CEO including speaking engagements, media opportunities, thought leadership, social media, writing opportunities, and member communication, among others – and staffing IFA leadership for various engagements accordingly

Review and edit organization-wide outbound communications materials, serving as an internal lead for review of any public facing materials
Advise on external communications to IFA staff and leadership

About Red Wing Arts

Since 1952, Red Wing Arts has connected people through creativity by providing exhibitions, education, festivals, concerts, public art, and arts experiences that strengthen our community.
Mission:
To build a vibrant community fueled by the arts by connecting, celebrating, inspiring, and leading through shared art experiences.
As Red Wing Arts continues to grow, we are investing in philanthropy as a strategic priority to ensure our long-term sustainability and expand our impact throughout the region.

Position Summary

The Director of Development leads Red Wing Arts' comprehensive development program in partnership with the Executive Director and Board of Directors.
This position is responsible for growing philanthropic support, strengthening relationships with donors and community partners, and building the systems and strategies that support the organization's long-term financial sustainability.
Success in this role is measured by stronger donor relationships, increased philanthropic investment, diversified revenue, effective fundraising systems, and the continued growth of Red Wing Arts' development program.

Areas of Responsibility

1. Build Relationships

Lead the organization's efforts to cultivate, solicit, and steward meaningful relationships with individuals, businesses, foundations, and community partners.
Success in this area includes:

Building and managing an active portfolio of donor and funding relationships.
Increasing donor engagement and long-term stewardship.
Expanding relationships with corporations, foundations, and community partners.
Partnering with the Executive Director and Board to strengthen major gift cultivation and donor engagement.

2. Build the Development Program

Develop, implement, and evaluate a comprehensive development strategy that supports the organization's mission and strategic goals.
Success in this area includes:

Developing and implementing an annual Development Plan.
Establishing fundraising priorities and measurable annual goals.
Growing annual giving, membership, corporate support, foundation funding, and major gifts.
Strengthening donor management systems and stewardship practices.
Building the organizational capacity needed for future comprehensive fundraising initiatives.

3. Strengthen Organizational Capacity

Provide leadership for the systems, communication, and collaboration that support successful fundraising across the organization.
Success in this area includes:

Coordinating grant proposals and reporting in collaboration with staff.
Maintaining accurate donor records and development reporting.
Supporting the Board Development Committee and fundraising efforts of Board members.
Collaborating with staff to communicate the impact of Red Wing Arts and inspire philanthropic investment.

Qualifications

The ideal candidate will bring many of the following qualifications:
Experience leading fundraising, philanthropy, nonprofit development, business development, or relationship management.
Demonstrated success building relationships and securing philanthropic support.
Experience developing and implementing fundraising strategies.
Experience with capital campaigns, including campaign planning, major gift cultivation, matching or challenge gifts, and campaign readiness.
Strong written, verbal, organizational, and interpersonal communication skills.
Experience working collaboratively with boards, volunteers, and community partners.
Knowledge of annual giving, major gifts, grants, corporate partnerships, donor stewardship, and fundraising best practices.

CFRE certification or comparable professional fundraising credentials are welcomed but not required.
We recognize that exceptional candidates bring a variety of professional experiences. If your background does not align perfectly with every qualification listed, but you believe you would thrive in this role and advance the mission of Red Wing Arts, we encourage you to apply.

What Success Looks Like

Within the first two years, the Director of Development will:
Implement a comprehensive Development Plan aligned with the organization's strategic priorities.
Strengthen donor engagement and stewardship practices.
Increase philanthropic support while diversifying contributed revenue.
Build systems that improve fundraising effectiveness and accountability.
Expand Red Wing Arts' long-term fundraising capacity through stronger relationships, sustainable practices, and strategic planning.

Job Description

USF Advancement connects the university with donors who want to make a difference by providing philanthropic support to promote student success, research, academic excellence and other strategic priorities. With an endowment that now exceeds $700 million in value, our dedicated team of approximately 200 professionals, including 60 fundraisers, encompasses alumni, development and foundation operations. The team is responsible for raising more than $150 million annually and has broken records year after year with more than $184 million raised in fiscal year 2025.

The Director of Development is a fundraising professional responsible for securing philanthropic support for Women in Leadership & Philanthropy (WLP) and strategic priorities across the University of South Florida.

Reporting directly to the Assistant Vice President for Affinity Programs and Executive Director of Women in Leadership & Philanthropy, this position is dedicated exclusively to development activities and serves as a key member of the USF Advancement team.

The Director of Development identifies, qualifies, cultivates, solicits, and closes major gifts from individuals, corporations, and foundations. The successful candidate will manage a portfolio of prospects and donors, develop meaningful relationships that advance donor engagement, and partner with university leadership to align philanthropic investments with institutional priorities.

Employees of USF Advancement live out the values of responsibility, innovation, service, and excellence in each of its highly collaborative departments. We use trusted data and ethical AI to enhance decision-making, strengthen engagement, and enable our teams to focus on what matters most: relationships and impact.

This position is primarily onsite and requires flexibility to meet with donors and prospects throughout the Tampa Bay region and beyond.

Responsibilities

Identify, cultivate, solicit and manage a portfolio of major gift prospects and donors ($50,000+) with a focus on securing significant philanthropic support for Women in Leadership & Philanthropy and the University of South Florida.
Identify and qualify new prospects through research, referrals, volunteer engagement, and personal outreach.
Conduct discovery, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship meetings with prospects and donors.
Develop and implement individualized strategies to move prospects through the donor pipeline from identification to gift commitment.
Collaborate with advancement colleagues and university stakeholders to identify philanthropic opportunities and align donor interests with institutional needs.
Prepare proposals, gift agreements and other donor communications that support fundraising objectives.
Maintain accurate records of prospect activity, strategy, and outcomes within university systems.
Meet established activity and fundraising goals, including visits, solicitations, proposal submissions, and gift commitments.
Represent the University of South Florida and Women in Leadership & Philanthropy at donor meetings, events, and community engagements as appropriate.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

This position requires Bachelor's degree and 5 years of experience related to development or other appropriate professional experience. Five to seven years demonstrated experience identifying, cultivating, soliciting, and closing major ($50,000+) philanthropic gifts is preferred.

The Director, Communications
is responsible for executing and supporting the day-to-day internal and external communications strategy and tactics for the International Franchise Association. This individual must possess a deep understanding of political and business communication, organizational priorities, and considerations surrounding a member-facing organization. This position will report to the vice president of communications while providing guidance to a team of communications specialists and external consultants.

Responsibilities

Production and editing of wide-ranging communications materials including communications plans, press releases, op-eds and articles, member communications, social media posts and content, visuals, scripts, speeches, talking points, and more
Drive communications strategy to support organizational priorities and promotion of the franchise business model
Build and maintain relationships with members of the media, regularly staying in touch with key reporters, proactively pitching ideas, closely monitoring current events and news cycles, and presenting media opportunities
Draft and oversee various IFA communications channels including newsletters, websites, columns, and social media in conjunction with IFA’s marketing team
Lead on executive communications and positioning for IFA President and CEO including speaking engagements, media opportunities, thought leadership, social media, writing opportunities, and member communication, among others – and staffing IFA leadership for various engagements accordingly
Stay apprised of media and social media trends, regularly suggesting ideas and best practices through continued education
Review and edit organization-wide outbound communications materials, serving as an internal lead for review of any public facing materials
Advise on external communications to IFA staff and leadership
Other duties as assigned, such as, but not limited to, photography, website management, social media management, video development and production, graphic and visual communication

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in communications, public relations, political science, or related field preferred.
Minimum 6-8 years’ experience in political communications, public affairs, or media relations/advocacy. Senior communications management role either in-house, with an agency, or on Capitol Hill preferred.
Minimum 5 years’ experience in media relations with a proven track record of established media contacts and results and demonstrated skill and comfort in proactively building relationships with target reporters.
Extensive successful writing and editing experience on complicated subject matter, with an ability to meet deadlines and turn projects quickly and free of errors. Must have a keen eye for detail.
Demonstrated experience and leadership in managing comprehensive strategic communications, media relations, and an external communications program to advance an organization’s mission and goals.
Ability to apply innovative and strategic thinking to plans; ability to apply excellent judgment and creative problem-solving skills; excellent negotiation and conflict-resolution skills.
Ability to make confident decisions on direction, anticipate and navigate changes in the environment as they occur, and understand the business climate and franchise business model.
Strong written and verbal communication skills; ability to speak confidently, persuasively, and effectively when interfacing with senior management, Board of Directors, and staff.
This position must be located in Washington, DC, with occasional travel.
